findings.summary: URN validation uses the raw string length helper instead of the manifest text-safety boundary.
findings.consequence: A 200 Reader manifest with a non-null URN containing C0/C1 controls, lone surrogates, or surrounding whitespace can pass the server manifest validator and be preserved as `ReaderManifestResponse`; the later production shortcut defensively drops those values, so the page can load with backend data that only fails when the user tries to copy the resolver URL.
findings.evidence: `optionalUrn` accepts `value === null || stringWithin(value, 100)`, while `manifestText` rejects untrimmed strings, C0/C1 controls, and lone surrogates. The validated `manifest.urn` is copied through `readerCommonMetadata` and the reader API response, then `urnResolverUrl` performs a second stricter check before building the resolver URL.
findings.recommendation: Validate URNs with `value === null || manifestText(value, 100)` and, if product semantics require real URNs, add the expected `urn:` shape there. That keeps the backend response boundary aligned with the later resolver URL boundary instead of accepting data that downstream code must discard.
